Team Sessions from $1,500

These are tried and true, ready to go, and I've run every one of them more times than I can count. You bring the space and the snacks, I bring the rest, and we're done in ninety minutes.

  • Point the Finger

    When everyone's working hard and things still go sideways.

    Your people care. They have good values and they're trying to do the right thing, and somehow it still turns into missed handoffs and finger-pointing. This hands-on session lets the whole team feel that moment together (it's funnier than it sounds), and then we talk about what's underneath it: fuzzy expectations, crossed wires about who owns what, and the conversations nobody wants to have. Your team leaves with a shared way to talk about accountability and one thing to change on Monday.

  • Hoops

    What does "good performance" mean here?

    Most teams are working hard toward a target nobody has quite put into words. This one starts with a challenge full of unknowns, the kind of goal you have to chase without a clear map, and then we use what happened to get on the same page: what good performance looks like here, how we'll know when we're hitting it, and how values and results fit together. Your team leaves with a definition they can work toward, and you leave with a clearer way to set expectations and have fair conversations about them.

  • Your Go-To Power Move

    What you reach for when the pressure spikes, and where you learned it.

    Every leader has a default lever they grab when things get tense: position, expertise, relationships, sheer force of personality. In this session leaders map where they learned theirs, which is usually long before they had a title, and then look honestly at how it shows up with their team today. It gets real fast. People walk out knowing their own default, where it stops working, and one other lever to practice. It pairs well with the Power Isn't a Dirty Word keynote.

The Strategy Session from $7,500

A strategy day built on what you can do, not what you can't.

Most strategy sessions start with what's broken. Mine starts with what's working, because that's the stuff you can build on. Grounded in appreciative inquiry, this full-day session gets everybody up and moving, and it gets everybody's thinking up on the wall, the owner's and the team's. By the end of the day your team agrees on what direction you're headed and walks out with a concrete plan for how to get there.

Most strategy fails in the follow-through, not the plan, so I offer quarterly check-ins to keep it moving.

Looking for a full multi-day strategic plan? I use the standard tools and make them something your team will want to show up for. Let's talk about it.
